summary.intent: Evaluate how well the wisp-plugins set served front-end work and design ideation across the techworx/orin-dx and pages projects, then (in later turns) strip ceremony from the plugins and tighten how ADRs are written so they are scannable, outcome-focused records.
summary.outcome: Four investigations found the plugins are spec-first, converge-only and have no visual/browser or sketch mode, so ideation ran outside them. Backstories were removed from 44 agents (ADR 017), ADRs 007-008 and 011-017 were condensed into one scannable layout with a warn-only style check, and an outcome-versus-baseline check was added, all pushed to trail #386.

repo: Only about 2 real top-level sessions exist per project dir; the other hundreds of jsonl files are subagent transcripts, so session counts are misleading.
Plugin agents were used in only a few sessions (orin-dx b8d16e96, pages 24655582, one vanguard run); smith reviewer/mutator/recon/exit-gate and sentinel were never used.
Gates check spec internal consistency, not rendered output; specs had no visual/layout criteria, so visual defects like NavSheet not full screen were caught only by the user's eye.
Specs were often retrofitted from prototypes and went stale; SPEC-013 superseded 26 of SPEC-001's criteria and 35 of SPEC-003c's 36.
Muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that does not exist, so implemented a11y is never checked.
Generated Codex output in dist/ goes stale when shared references change; run `just marketplace-sync` (and `just claude-manifests-sync`) before `just check`.
Changing plugins that shipped in a released version needs a patch bump plus a new changelog entry, not an edit to the released entry.
ADR style is enforced by scripts/check-adr-style.py (warn-only, runs in just check) and tests/test_adr_style.py; docs/adr/README.md index rows and tests/test_navigator_plan.py pin ADR content.

code.finding: Only UI-aware agent: requires props, variants, states and a11y criteria, but rejects appearance-based criteria as leakage and has no visual intent channel.
Names a 'render' boundary only as a label; recording 'render unexercised' as a coverage gap lets UI changes pass.
Smith accepts a spec@1 with no plan, but still runs recon, mutator, reviewer and a binding exit-gate; there is no spike mode.
Rigidity language: blockers-only resubmission and spec persisted only after gate pass; related caps at L154, L162.

friction: Large 60-130 KB spec/plan files stalled agents; 17 failed agent tasks and 32 stall mentions.
Exit-gate loops were non-monotonic, with wording-only blockers and some caused by the previous round's prescribed fix (e.g. SPEC-001 needed 13 verdicts, 10 fails).
Design decisions were lost across sessions (page-width decision), frustrating the user.
Initial ADR length threshold of 350 words flagged nearly everything, so it was recalibrated to 450 and then to 600.
A test padding was too short for the threshold, and just check failed on stale generated Codex output until re-synced.
GitHub returned transient server errors on push and needed retries; the subagent fetch needed network allowlisting.
My first session count (~810) was wrong because subagent transcripts were counted as sessions.
Subagent added invented content (revisit trigger for ADR 007) that had to be removed.
open_items: Trail #386 needs approval and the three Entire findings need resolving.
Design doc docs/design/agent-native-architecture.md was still being written and needs review.
Repo calls pending: Caliper's hard-coded rustup path, Pages' rtk rule, orin-dx-site's status.
Not started pending user approval: TokenEconomizer trial (writes Claude settings) and collapsing build-side chains (muse into scribe, courier scripts).
Gaps identified but not built: sketch/spike mode, visual exploration agent, browser/screenshot capability, prototype-to-spec path, decision log across sessions.
Outcome-versus-baseline convention is prompt-level only with no runtime enforcement.
ADR 007/008 have no ADR-evidence entries in the implementation log; evidence pointers are commit hashes.
